rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 199 sets the rule that trade-imports-performance-tests joins a row when that row breaks what its k6 scripts use, and ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 2 says which repos change is worked out from the evidence, not fixed in advance; claim 200's 'no other row' rests only on its stated reason (the documents move is dropped) and only weighed route moves, so applying claim 199's rule to the perftests evidence brings the suite into each row whose change breaks a k6 script.
outcome: trade-imports-performance-tests changes in each increment whose change breaks one of its k6 scripts, on that increment's branch name, and nowhere else beyond inc-129. The row carrying req-095 changes the suite's commodity search from 'Cow' to 'Cattle' and the row carrying req-118 walks the main import reason page between the commodity page and Commodity details (req-1761). The increment that brings in the address book's category tabs makes the setup and session searches ask for the tab their address's type lands on and adds up the four tabs' results lines for the background-volume count, its seeded addresses each carrying one type so none is counted twice; every route and hook the suite reads is kept (req-1860, req-1861). The increment that adds the 'Choose an address type' step and the uses question makes the k6 add and background-volume scenarios choose 'Origin or Consignor', tick 'Place of origin' and accept the filtered list return, keeping today's field names; the edit scenario is unchanged (req-1870). The amend increment makes the k6 amendment check expect the amend review; cancel-amend keeps its route and ?cancelled=1, and resubmission already goes through the review and declaration (req-1877). Claim 200 is read by its own reason: no row moves the documents page, so no row needs the suite for that.
